parts.problem_md:
Fig. 4.1 shows the reaction pathway diagrams for two reactions.

![Two energy profile diagrams: reaction 1 shows reactants higher than products with labelled activation energy; reaction 2 shows reactants lower than products](assets/001-two-energy-profile-diagrams-reaction-1-shows-rea.png)

The activation energy for reaction 1 is represented by the arrow E<sub>a</sub>.

(i) Define activation energy.

[1]

(ii) On Fig. 4.1, draw and label an arrow to show the activation energy for reaction 2.

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - (i) The minimum energy that colliding particles must have to react **[1 mark]**
> - (ii) Arrow drawn to show E<sub>a</sub> on the diagram, as shown **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> On energy profile diagrams, activation energy is always measured from the reactants' energy level up to the peak — not from zero or from the products' level.

parts.problem_md:
During reaction 2, the temperature of the reaction mixture changes.

State how the temperature changes.

Give a reason for your answer.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Temperature decreases, because the reaction is endothermic (takes in thermal energy; the products have more energy than the reactants) **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Link the direction of temperature change directly to the energy profile shape — if products are higher than reactants, energy is taken in from the surroundings, so temperature falls.

parts.problem_md:
The electrolysis shown in Fig. 4.1 produces the alkali sodium hydroxide.

Aqueous sodium hydroxide reacts with dilute sulfuric acid.

(i) Complete the word equation for this reaction.

![Diagram of a word equation: sodium hydroxide plus sulfuric acid arrow blank box plus blank box, for students to fill in the reaction products.](assets/002-diagram-of-a-word-equation-sodium-hydroxide-plus.png)

[1]

(ii) The reaction between aqueous sodium hydroxide and dilute sulfuric acid is exothermic.

State what is meant by an exothermic reaction.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
(i)

![Text equation showing sodium hydroxide plus sulfuric acid arrow producing sodium sulfate and water, illustrating a neutralisation reaction](assets/003-text-equation-showing-sodium-hydroxide-plus-sulf.png)

**[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - (ii) An exothermic reaction transfers thermal energy to the surroundings **[1 mark]**
> - (ii) This leads to an increase in temperature of the surroundings **[1 mark]**
> 
> Idea of the surroundings may be seen in either marking point

> **[exam-tip]**
> A common mistake is describing energy changes only in terms of the reacting chemicals — always mention the surroundings when defining exothermic or endothermic reactions.
